Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call today - appreciate the time. Quick recap from our side and a few asks ahead of the deeper technical session:

Pain points / goals:
- User-facing inference latency is inconsistent; we need predictable 95th percentile latency for chat flows (goal: <= 350ms for ~256 token responses).
- Peak throughput spikes during morning reports: ~150-220 requests/sec sustained for 5-10 minutes.
- Cost is a concern: want to balance model quality with predictable unit economics.
- Must run inside our AWS us-west-2 VPC (private deployment) with KMS-managed keys; SOC2 evidence required.

Model requirements:
- Prefer a fine-tuned Llama2-class model (quality target similar to current internal 13B baseline), but open to larger model if latency/throughput are acceptable.
- Max sequence length ~2048 tokens, typical prompt+response 300-800 tokens.

Topology constraints:
- Private deployment behind our ALB; traffic routed from API gateway.
- Need autoscaling but with predictable warmup/cold-starts.

Attachments: I attached a short perf snapshot from last week (nimble_perf_snapshot.csv) and a basic architecture diagram (nimble_arch_diagram.png).

Next steps: can you share a short recap of proposed topology and which Redwood model variants you think are a fit? Also would like to schedule a deep technical session with your infra/SRE folks next week.

Best,
Alex

Alex - thanks for the perf snapshot and diagram. Quick recap from our technical discovery + proposed next steps so we go into the deep-dive aligned.

Summary of pain points we heard:
- Target: stable P95 latency goal in the 300-350ms range for common chat responses (~256 tokens).
- Traffic profile: short bursts up to ~220 req/s, baseline ~30-40 req/s.
- Private deployment + KMS required; SOC2 evidence requested.
- Concern about cold-starts and unpredictable batching impact on tail latency.

Proposed Redwood approach (high level):
- Deployment: Redwood Private (VPC) in us-west-2 using a Dedicated GPU pool attached to your VPC.
- Model variants: primary: Llama2-70B quantized (4-bit/awq) for quality; fallback: Llama2-13B quantized for high-load graceful degradation.
- Autoscaling & topology: 2 initial GPU pods (N+1), autoscale to handle sustained bursts. Use smart routing to shift traffic to 13B variant when contention exceeds configured thresholds.
- Latency optimizations: continuous batching with a 20ms batching window, KV prefix caching for repeated prompts, and warm pools to avoid cold-starts for critical routes.
- Monitoring: expose per-route P50/P90/P95 latency, request queue depth, batch sizes, GPU utilization, and per-token cost.

Risks / open questions:
- 70B quality vs cost/latency tradeoff - we should validate via a quick perf/quality pilot.
- Quantization artifacts - we recommend running a small eval suite for your critical prompts.
- Networking: need your egress/ingress constraints and whether you prefer PrivateLink or VPC peering for control-plane communications.

Next steps / ask list:
1) Schedule a 60-90 minute technical deep-dive with your infra, SRE, and model owners. Rishi and Dev will join.
2) Share your expected 15/60/95 minute traffic profiles (we received the perf snapshot but a short CSV with minute-level counts would help).
3) We'll provide a proposed topology PDF and an initial cost/latency projection for both 70B and 13B variants.

I'll attach the proposed topology diagram (redwood_proposed_topology.pdf) to this thread.

Thanks - looking forward to the deep dive.

- Marissa

Alex - quick technical clarifications ahead of the session so we can prep focused material:

1) Latency targets: you listed P95 <= 350ms for ~256 tokens. To be conservative we should plan for P95 <= 300ms target on the 70B-quantized path for 256 token responses; if that looks tight we'll recommend the 13B primary with 70B as a quality tier.

2) Batching/windowing: we typically use a 20ms batching window for steady-state traffic - this gives good throughput without blowing up tail latency for chat. For bursty traffic we recommend pre-warmed pools and a shorter window on critical routes.

3) KV cache & session affinity: repeated prompts benefit from prefix/KV caching. We'll need session affinity for chat sessions you want cached across requests; otherwise cache hit rates will be low.

4) Warm-up strategy: on autoscale events we recommend a warm pool of idle workers that can be promoted quickly; full model warm-up actions (e.g., KV cache priming) are part of the runbook.

5) Observability: please make sure you can expose trace IDs and sample payloads (redacted) so we can map latency to model/infra events during the pilot.

I'll prepare a short runbook and perf comparison table for 70B vs 13B (latency/cost per 1k tokens) for the deep dive.

- Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
